Wait, workers read those docs (records exist). But now 404. Maybe document service only holds documents for the current job? But equipment 1/2 quotes accessible? Odd. Maybe document service is dynamically scoped: each worker can only access docs associated with its job, plus globally shared equipment quote docs? Let's analyze.

Our worker read RECOVERY-000003-requisition, storage 000003 quote, budget 000003. Other workers read their own requisitions, storage quotes, budgets. When I, worker-6c..., try to read 000001/2 budget/storage quote, 404 because not associated with my job. But equipment 000001/2 quotes are 200 because perhaps they are global docs? Hmm, why would they be global? Maybe because other workers requested them, making them accessible? Or because supplier quotes are shared across sites by design, while requisitions/budgets/storage quotes are job-scoped? That doesn't make sense.

Maybe document service access control: documents are accessible if:
- associated with current job (requisition, storage quote, budget)
- or document request exists in shared registry for it (equipment quotes 1/2)
So once DR-000030 and DR-000033 exist (created by other workers), their requested documents are accessible to us. Our DR-000028 also exists but document 000003 still 404. Why? Maybe because request's status open but doc not available yet. Could be because the request's creator must attach? Or because requested doc only becomes accessible if it is physically added by an external source. Perhaps 000001/2 docs existed but were hidden until requested; 000003 doc truly missing.

Wait, read-116/117 bytes 243 vs storage 241. Equipment quotes are 243 bytes because vendor/sku longer. So likely documents exist.

Let's test accessing a different job's equipment quote after request: we did 200. Try 000004 equipment quote (no request). If 404, then request gating. Try RECOVERY-000002-requisition (no request? worker read it but no request). 404. So access to other-job requisitions denied, but equipment quotes maybe globally visible if requested. Try "Recovery Equipment 000004-quote.json" to see.
